new_statements.quote: [p.779 §8] Las raíces son monosílabas o bisílabas. Son los morfemas principales. Llevan un acento prosódico muy ligero al principio que se conserva siempre en su lugar de origen aunque estén acompañadas de prefijos. En las raíces monosílabas, además de llevar el acento prosódico, la vocal se alarga más o menos al doble aunque tenga un solo tono. [...] [p.777 §5] En las raíces bisílabas, la vocal de la primera sílaba, la que lleva el acento prosódico, no se alarga [...]. Para el hablante nativo, tanto el acento prosódico como la duración de vocales son fáciles de predecir, y por tal motivo no las señalamos en la ortografía. [p.778 §7, los determinantes] Son de una sílaba, sin acento prosódico, con una vocal corta como elemento central.
new_statements.translation: Roots are monosyllabic or disyllabic. They are the principal morphemes. They carry a very light prosodic accent at their beginning, which always stays in its original place even when prefixes accompany them. In monosyllabic roots, besides carrying the prosodic accent, the vowel is lengthened to roughly double even if it has a single tone. [...] In disyllabic roots the vowel of the first syllable, the one that carries the prosodic accent, is not lengthened [...]. For the native speaker both the prosodic accent and vowel length are easy to predict, and for that reason we do not mark them in the orthography. [Determinants = prefixes, bound pronouns, particles] are monosyllabic, without prosodic accent, with a short vowel as nucleus.
new_statements.citation: Anderson, E. Richard & Hilario Concepción Roque. 1983. Diccionario cuicateco: español-cuicateco, cuicateco-español. (Serie de vocabularios y diccionarios indígenas 'Mariano Silva y Aceves' 26.) México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. Apéndice A 'Fonología y ortografía'.
new_statements.locator: Apéndice A, §8 'Raíces' p. 779 (PDF p. 800); with §5 p. 777 (PDF p. 798) and §7 'Determinantes' p. 778 (PDF p. 799)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened the page renders (printed p. 779, sec. 8 'Raices'), -p. 777, sec. 5 'Duracion de las Vocales y Acento Prosodico') and -p. 778, sec. 7 'Determinantes') of Anderson & Concepcion Roque 1983 (scan held by the project). Every quoted sentence is there word for word: p. 779 'Las raices son monosilabas o bisilabas. Son los morfemas principales. Llevan un acento prosodico muy ligero al principio que se conserva siempre en su lugar de origen aunque esten acompanadas de prefijos. En las raices monosilabas, ademas de llevar el acento prosodico, la vocal se alarga mas o menos al doble aunque tenga un solo tono.'; p. 777 'En las raices bisilabas, la vocal de la primera silaba, la que lleva…
new_statements.rule_in_words: A light, predictable word accent falls on the first syllable of the root (roots are (C)V or (C)VCV); it does not shift when prefixes/proclitic 'determinantes' are added, and those elements are never stressed. So prefix+monosyllabic-root words are final-stressed, bare disyllabic roots initial-stressed. Tone (4 levels) is the contrastive prosody; accent is not.
new_statements.exceptions: Apparent CV²CV¹⁴ forms (y'a²ti¹⁴ 'simple', nd'i²cu¹⁴ 'viejo') are explained as compounds with an added tone-4 morpheme, not accent exceptions; the pair cu³ndú¹ 'voy a cardar' (accent on penult: c- + root -u³ndu¹) vs cu⁴ndú²¹ 'voy a montar' (accent on final: cu⁴ + root ndu²¹) shows accent diagnosing the root; Spanish loans keep Spanish stress, realised as fixed tone patterns (pp. 784-785).
new_statements.domain_note: Root/word domain: accent is a property of the root-initial syllable and survives prefixation; illustrated both in citation forms and short verb phrases. CAUTION (identity): the description is of Santa María Pápalo Cuicatec, which ISO 639-3/Ethnologue/SIL catalogue as Tepeuxila Cuicatec [cux] = Glottolog sant1437 under tepe1280; only Glottolog's bibliography attaches this book to teut1235. No stress statement was found for Teutila-proper speech (San Pedro Teutila / San Andrés Teotilalpam).
new_statements.identity_note: All three first-hand stress statements located (Anderson & Concepción Roque 1983; Prewett & Prewett 1972; Needham & Davis 1946) describe Santa María Pápalo or Concepción Pápalo speech. ISO 639-3 / Ethnologue 16 ('Cuicatec, Tepeuxila [cux].. Dialects: Santa María Pápalo') and the SIL archive catalogue both file these under Tepeuxila Cuicatec [cux]; Glottolog has Santa María Pápalo as dialect sant1437 under tepe1280, yet Glottolog 5.1's bibliography attaches the 1983 dictionary to teut1235 (which is why it appears in this target's ref list). The tepe1280 check already uses Anderson 1983, so adopting it here would list one variety under two glottocodes. Teutila-proper (cut: San Pedro Teutila, San Andrés/Santa Cruz Teotilalpam, Santa María Tlalixtac; 'northern/eastern' INALI variants) has open material only in the form of López 1958 word lists; its one modern description (Ariano 2023, San Andrés Teotilálpam consonant system) is print-only.

sources.locator: Apéndice A, §8 'Raíces' p. 779 (PDF p. 800); with §5 p. 777 (PDF p. 798) and §7 'Determinantes' p. 778 (PDF p. 799)
sources.note: pp. 777-779 §§5,7,8: roots (mono- or disyllabic) carry a very light 'acento prosódico' at their beginning which stays in place when prefixes are added; 'determinantes' (prefixes, bound pronouns, particles) are monosyllabic and unstressed; monosyllabic roots lengthen; accent and length are predictable and left unwritten; minimal pair cu³ndú¹ (penult accent, root -u³ndu¹) vs cu⁴ndú²¹ (final accent, root ndu²¹). Spanish loans: stress position mapped onto tone patterns (pp. 784-785). Variety: Santa María Pápalo (ISO/SIL/Ethnologue = Tepeuxila cux; Glottolog sant1437 under tepe1280).

sources.note: p. 46 (San Juan Tepeuxila = tepe1280): 'As for stress, it is trochaic and falls on the second mora starting at the right boundary of the stem (Mendoza 2024)', e.g. [ðu3ˈtuː34] 'hill' vs [ˈni4nũː4] 'corn'; stress is the strongest predictor of tonal variation. Mentions San Andrés/Santa Cruz Teotilalpam only for tonal variants (p. 60) and cites Ariano 2023 for San Andrés Teotilálpam consonants.

sources.note: p. 140: 'Stress is not phonemic. However, the conditions for placement are still not too clear. A stress appears to fall on the first syllable of most morphemes, with possible placement on a high tone at the end of a morpheme.' Concepción Pápalo = Tepeuxila (tepe1280), not Teutila.

sources.note: §7.1 p. 95: 'Stress has not been written since it does not seem to play an important role in the segmental phonology.' §7.3 p. 96: 'It is not clear from our present data whether stress is phonemic. Evidence that it might be non-phonemic is the absence of pairs of words that differ only by stress, and the preponderance of stressed syllables which have high tone.. If stress is non-phonemic, it is conditioned by factors other than tone alone.' No position rule. Santa María Pápalo (cux).
